title: Where does my money go?

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you know how much you spent last week? Guess: who in this episode once had no money for a whole month — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: Saving for later

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is money — and I have to start with a sad student story.
[laugh] Another one?
My first month at university, I got my student loan and I felt rich. New trainers, restaurants every night, taxis everywhere.
Oh no. I know where this is going.
By the fifteenth, my account was empty. I lived on toast and pasta for two weeks. [sigh] I couldn't even afford the bus.
So you had to tighten your belt.
Very tight. And I borrowed money from my friends, so I had debt too. It was a terrible feeling.
That's how many people learn. My parents taught me to make a budget when I was a teenager.
How does your budget work?
It's simple. When I get my salary, I divide it: first rent and bills, then food and transport, then savings, and what's left is for fun.
Savings before fun? That's very Leyla.
[chuckle] Yes! If I wait until the end of the month, there's nothing to save.
Fair. And prices go up every year now. Inflation makes everything harder.
True. Coffee costs almost double what it did five years ago.
So now I live on a shoestring when I can. I cook at home and take my lunch to work.
Good. And are you thinking about the future? Like an investment?
A small one. Every month I put a little into a savings plan. It doesn't break the bank, but it grows.
That's the secret, I think. Small amounts, but every month.
And don't buy things to feel happy. That feeling lasts ten minutes.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is something you saved money for — and was it worth it?
Mine was a bike. Totally worth it. See you next time!
Bye for now!
